Title: unpreventable damage vs flesh of marble

Messages.Author: Alanmut
Messages.Body:
I have a question: the Flesh of Marble card says that the vampire takes the first damage and the rest is prevented, but what about cases of unpreventable damage? Since the card describes the "prevent" effect, does that mean the unpreventable effect applies normally?

Alanmut

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Alanmut wrote:
> I have a question: the Flesh of Marble card says that the vampire takes the first damage and the rest is prevented, but what about cases of unpreventable damage? Since the card describes the "prevent" effect, does that mean the unpreventable effect applies normally?
>
> Alanmut
>
Unpreventable damage cannot be prevented. FoM prevents damage, so it doesn't work against unpreventable damage.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: DavidR
Messages.Body:
so if on a given round a vampire with flesh of marble was assigned 2 unpreventable damage and 4 other damage, he take 3 damage (2 unpreventable and another to activate the FoM) or one of unpreveantable damage can activate the FoM and in this case he took only 2 (unpreventable) damage?

David Resende - Prince of Teresina

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:

> so if on a given round a vampire with flesh of marble was assigned 2 unpreventable damage and 4 other damage, he take 3 damage (2 unpreventable and another to activate the FoM) or one of unpreveantable damage can activate the FoM and in this case he took only 2 (unpreventable) damage?

The vampire's choice, provided that all damage is inflicted together (no first strike involved for instance).
